Bringing AI Into Your Organization

Thank the organizers and everyone in the audience for being here.

This is my experience—your mileage may vary.

Just as the cloud changed the way many organizations operate, AI will too. How AI changes the way organizations operate is what I am focused on.

FROM HYPE
TO REALITY.

2 / 25
SLIDE 02 / 25

The hype cycle

Frontier providers have crossed disillusionment. Early adopters have moved beyond novelty into operationalization. Many builders and consumers are still near the peak of expectations. Where is our organization on this curve?

EVERYONE
HAS A
TAKE.

3 / 25
SLIDE 03 / 25

Everyone has a take

Competing stories shape the conversation:

  • Acceleration: capability is rising quickly and threatens cognitive work.
  • Historical skepticism: technological disruption also creates opportunities.
  • Meaning and trust: the challenge is reorganizing institutions, not just adopting tools.
  • The agentic economy: coordination and discovery become infrastructure.
  • Underuse: using AI more creates new capacity, enablement, and innovation challenges.
✓ ACCESS✓ DEMOS! CONTROLS? STRATEGY

THE MODEL
IS NOT THE
BOTTLENECK.

Changing behavior is hard.
4 / 25
SLIDE 04 / 25

The model is not the bottleneck

Models and impressive demos are widely available. Leadership wants strategy; security wants controls; employees want to know what they can do. Licenses are easy. Changed behavior is hard. The bottleneck is increasingly not the model.

LAYERS OF
CHANGE.

5 / 25
SLIDE 05 / 25

Layers of change

AI changes the operating model before most organizations recognize it.

Organization: Can we build a dependable capability?

Team: Can we coordinate effectively?

Individual: What work is valuable now?

Security runs through every layer, rather than sitting beside them.

THE ORG.

6 / 25
SLIDE 06 / 25

The organization

Begin with the organization. What has to change for AI to become part of normal work?

AI HAS THREE GATES.

01Adoption
02Capacity
03Innovation
7 / 25
SLIDE 07 / 25

Three gates

Organizations often collapse three different challenges into one word: adoption.

Adoption: Will people actually use it?

Capacity: Can we do it repeatedly?

Innovation: Will we change what we do?

ADOPTION
THEATER.

8 / 25
SLIDE 08 / 25

Adoption theater

Adoption theater: steering committees, acceptable-use policies, Copilot licenses, training, hackathons, chatbot pilots, and strategy documents. These activities alone do not show that work has changed.

TUESDAY
AFTERNOON.

9 / 25
SLIDE 09 / 25

The Tuesday test

Look for people working differently on an ordinary Tuesday afternoon. Multiple roles change their workflows because a new tool exists. New capabilities become possible. That is evidence of actual progress.

DO YOU
BELIEVE?

10 / 25
SLIDE 10 / 25

The Moneyball question

Have you seen Moneyball? It is often remembered as a tribute to statistics, computing, and data science. But the central conflict is belief: do you believe the signal enough to act on it?

Recall the exchange: ‘Do you believe in this thing or not?’ ‘I do.’ Then the insistence that they do not need to explain themselves to everyone.

FROM DATA
TO CHANGED WORK.

Discover
Believe
Decide
Act
Rebuild
11 / 25
SLIDE 11 / 25

Evidence into action

Better information is only the start. See the signal, believe it, put it into decisions, act against established intuition, and reorganize around the capability. This is why Moneyball is an adoption story.

12 / 25
SLIDE 12 / 25

Capacity is repeatability

Gate two: capacity. Use Shia and ‘over and over and over again’ to emphasize repetition. A successful demonstration is not yet a capability the organization can depend on.

FROM DEMO
TO CAPABILITY.

01Demo
02Workflow
03System
04Dependable
13 / 25
SLIDE 13 / 25

From demo to capability

Demo: Can this work?

Workflow: Can people use it in real work?

System: Can we support and govern it?

Dependable capability: Can we rely on it repeatedly?

Capacity means moving through these stages.

GATE 3:
Adoption: Faster report
Capacity: Automated report
Innovation: Why this report?

WHY?

14 / 25
SLIDE 14 / 25

Innovation is asking why

Adoption: I write the report faster.

Capacity: AI builds the report.

Innovation: Why does this report exist?

The third gate asks whether the work itself should change.

The team

Code

16 / 25
SLIDE 16 / 25

Output rises, attention remains finite

AI increases code, writing, analysis, ideas, messages, and artifacts. Human input/output capacity and organizational attention remain finite. The bottleneck moves from production to coordination.

MORE INFORMATION
≠ MORE COORDINATION.

17 / 25
SLIDE 17 / 25

Information is not coordination

AI is an extraordinary radio-traffic generator.

Information is not communication; communication is not coordination; coordination is not action.

A thousand alerts are not awareness. A thousand findings are not a security program. A thousand recommendations are not strategy.

Teams need shared intent, clear roles, priorities, situational awareness, and communication discipline.

CULTURE
EATS
STRATEGY
EATS
EVERYTHING ELSE

18 / 25
SLIDE 18 / 25

Culture eats strategy eats everything else

Culture eats strategy eats everything else. Connect the claim to everyday behavior: what people actually do shapes whether a strategy gets carried out.

As output gets cheaper, clear intent matters more: What are we trying to accomplish? What matters most? What will we not pursue? What can people decide locally, and what requires escalation?

The individual

Move to the individual. As production becomes cheaper, what happens to an individual's craft and contribution?

WHAT IS
VALUABLE

20 / 25
SLIDE 20 / 25

What is valuable work now?

Picture a software engineer sitting at a desk. What does the engineer actually do? Whatever the answer, that craft is changing. Which parts of the work are becoming cheap, and which parts remain valuable?

THE HUMAN
ADVANTAGE.

01Craft
02Taste
03Judgment
04Purpose
21 / 25
SLIDE 21 / 25

Craft, taste, judgment, purpose

Craft: Can I make the thing?

Taste: Can I recognize what good looks like?

Judgment: Can I choose correctly?

Purpose: Do I understand why we are making it?

AI expands capacity, but purpose remains deeply organizational and human.

THE OPERATING
MODEL.

22 / 25
SLIDE 22 / 25

Put it together

Bring organization, team, and individual together as one operating model. Organizational capability depends on team coordination and individual judgment. Security runs through the whole system.

ON MONDAY,
ASK THIS.

WHERE IS YOUR
BOTTLENECK NOW?

GatesCapacityCoordinationAuthorityTaste
23 / 25
SLIDE 23 / 25

Questions for Monday

Where is your bottleneck now?

Organization: Which gate are we at? Are we building capacity?

Team: Are we measuring capability or output? Where does coordination break down? Is strategy clear, and where is authority moving?

Individual: What work is becoming cheap? What taste is valuable? How are people learning AI?

Consider what new connections and security needs emerge.

WHAT KIND
OF ORGANIZATION
WILL YOU
BECOME?

24 / 25
SLIDE 24 / 25

What kind of organization will you become?

The interesting question is not whether your organization adopts AI. It is what kind of organization you become once it does.
